name: SWE-rebench
description: A public dataset of more than 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks, designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches. The dataset is constructed using a scalable, fully automated pipeline for mining real-world software engineering tasks from GitHub repositories.
license: Permissive licenses including MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-4-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, CC0-1.0, ZPL-2.1, and other manually verified permissive licenses
citeAs: Badertdinov et al., SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents, NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is collected through a fully automated, four-stage pipeline: (1) preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories, (2) automated installation instruction configuration using LLM-driven approaches, (3) execution-based installation verification in containerized environments, and (4) automated quality assessment using fine-tuned LLMs. The pipeline downloads approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, from over 30,000 Python repositories with permissive licenses.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Automated Data Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data is sourced from GitHub Archive (JSON archives of public GitHub events) and GitHub repositories (cloned with full commit histories). Primary sources include issues, pull requests, commit histories, and repository metadata from Python repositories where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase lines of code.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025. The pipeline enables continuous collection of fresh tasks, with the benchmark continuously updated to include tasks from 2025 onwards.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Pull requests are divided into solution patches (changes to non-test files) and test patches (changes to test files only). Patches are generated by diffing head_commit against base_commit to isolate changes made directly within the PR branch. If head_commit is unavailable, merge_commit is used as fallback. Test directives are filtered to exclude deleted files. Versions are normalized to major.minor format (e.g., 1.2.3 to 1.2) for environment grouping.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Multiple filtering stages are applied: (1) Issues must be from Python repositories with permissive licenses, marked as resolved, with merged PRs not linked to multiple issues, and issue descriptions longer than 10 characters. (2) PRs must introduce or modify tests and include code changes beyond test files, affecting 1 to 15 files. (3) Test execution logs must be free of critical errors (AttributeError, ImportError). (4) For benchmark subset: number of modified files ≤3, patch size ≤500 words, problem statement 16-1000 words in English, created in 2025, LLM-assessed difficulty <3, fail-to-pass tests ≤50. After filtering, approximately 153,400 potential task instances remain from initial 450,000, with final dataset containing 21,336 validated tasks.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated quality assessment is performed using a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model trained on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified. The model predicts three binary quality labels for each task: (1) Issue Clarity - whether the GitHub issue description is sufficiently detailed for a developer to understand and solve the problem, (2) Task Complexity - estimated effort to resolve the issue considering reasoning, code modification, and codebase familiarity, (3) Test Patch Correctness - whether tests accurately verify the intended fix without over-reliance on specific implementation details. Each task instance is assessed independently for each quality characteristic.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The fine-tuned quality assessment model achieved the following performance on validation set (413 examples from SWE-bench Verified, 75/25 train/validation split): Task Complexity - 81% accuracy, weighted F1: 0.82 (100 high-score vs. 313 low-score examples); Test Patch Correctness - 67% accuracy, weighted F1: 0.65 (180 high-score vs. 233 low-score examples); Issue Clarity - 79% accuracy, weighted F1: 0.76 (84 high-score vs. 329 low-score examples). While this automated assessment is not perfect, these labels offer users a means to filter the dataset and select task instances according to their specific criteria.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Three quality labels per task instance: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified annotations for quality assessment. Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct used for generating installation recipes and identifying relevant files. TractoAI platform used for distributed container building and parallel execution of verification tasks.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset uses continuous supply of fresh tasks collected using the automated pipeline. The benchmark is continuously updated with new tasks from recent GitHub issues. Dependency versions are frozen and recorded (via pip freeze, conda env export) after successful setup to ensure reproducibility. The leaderboard is continuously updated with new model evaluations. Versioning information tracks creation dates of issues and pull requests against model release dates to explicitly mark potentially contaminated evaluations.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and benchmark aim to accelerate open-source research in LLM-based software engineering agents by providing large-scale training data and decontaminated evaluation. However, this progress brings potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is currently limited exclusively to Python projects, restricting immediate applicability to other language ecosystems. The fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue description, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. The automated quality assessment, while scalable, cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment. Some failure modes during validation include: flaky tests with external API calls or floating-point precision issues, lack of interactivity during installation for older projects, and unpinned/obsolete dependencies. The LLM-based approach to generating installation recipes was validated on a limited set of 18 repositories and may not capture every project's subtleties.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for: (1) Training LLM-based software engineering agents, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning approaches that require interactive tasks with automatic verification mechanisms, (2) Benchmarking and evaluation of LLM-based agents in realistic SWE scenarios through the continuously updated SWE-rebench leaderboard, (3) Research on agentic software engineering with decontaminated, standardized evaluation. The benchmark uses a fixed ReAct-style agentic framework with identical prompts and default generation hyperparameters for all models to enable fair comparison of core model capabilities. Each model is evaluated five times on the full benchmark to account for stochasticity, with both standard error of the mean (SEM) and pass@5 metrics reported.
